clinical_profiles.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

patient_info.stressor: After Dennis was fired from his retail job following a dispute over sales procedures and missed merchandising targets, he initially tried to turn the loss into a competitive comeback plan, mapping out job leads, woodworking sales ideas, and district-manager ambitions from his coffee-shop chess table. During the following 3 weeks, his response became clinically significant as his mood and energy rose beyond his usual laid-back style, his sleep need dropped, his speech and thoughts sped up, and he began having vivid hallucinatory experiences, before shifting into a depressed state with little interest in fishing, vinyl hunting, tailgating, or home-brewing. Although he avoided hospitalization, the episode impaired his ability to search for work, keep appointments, manage bills, and maintain his usual routines, and he developed recurrent thoughts of death without taking action on them. He sought help himself at a community behavioral-health clinic after a church acquaintance mentioned walk-in services and he realized he could not explain or control what had happened over those 3 weeks.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: When I was all wound up, I heard my old store manager's voice clear as day over an intercom telling me to 'move the display,' even when I was sitting alone in my kitchen.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: After that burst of energy wore off, I felt like somebody had pulled the plug on me, and I would sit at the table staring at my coffee feeling empty and ashamed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I quit caring about the things that usually settle me down, like fishing, digging through vinyl records, tailgating, or checking on my home-brew, and they just felt like chores.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Most days lately I have to remind myself to eat, and my jeans are looser because supper just sits there looking like too much trouble.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Even when I do sleep now, I wake up before daylight with my stomach tight and my mind already on bills and what I messed up.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: I came in because I keep catching myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn't wake up, though I haven't made any plan to hurt myself.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Right after I got fired I felt oddly fired up, like I was going to prove everybody wrong, but I was also snapping at people over little things at the coffee shop.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: I was bouncing from job applications to sketching woodworking projects to rewriting my resume, hardly sitting still long enough to finish one thing before starting the next.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: For a while I honestly believed I could walk into any store in the district and run it better than the managers there, like losing my job had somehow made me the expert.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: There were several nights I only slept two or three hours and still got up feeling like I had a full tank and no reason to slow down.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: People at the chess table kept telling me to take a breath because once I started explaining my comeback plan, the words just kept pouring out.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: My thoughts were jumping so fast from sales numbers to job leads to beer recipes to old arguments that I couldn't keep hold of one idea for more than a few seconds.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: The only time I heard that store-manager voice or felt unreal certain I could take over any store was during those wired weeks after I got fired. Once I crashed into the low spell, the voice stopped and I was left embarrassed by what I had believed.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I fell behind on bills, missed callbacks and appointments, and could not keep a steady job search going even though I needed work. My usual routines at home got sloppy enough that I knew I could not just handle it by willpower.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: That high-energy, out-of-control stretch lasted about three weeks after I was fired.

depressive_episode_duration.name: Depressive Episode Duration
depressive_episode_duration.manifestation: The low spell has been hanging on for about three months since that crash.
